turn_text: We're talking with Ohio Republican Congressman Steve Shabbat, he's chairman of the House Small Business Committee. And sir, one of the complaints we did hear from some business experts in response to the tax cuts, especially on the small business side, but even on some of the others as well, is that there's still too much complexity going on here. It wasn't simplified as much as it could be. And so there's some good things, some bad things here, whether we're talking about pass-throughs or we're talking about other businesses perhaps that pay on the individual scale and so forth. What's your thoughts on what was dealt with in terms of complexity and what can still be done better?

Well, I agree with the criticism that there wasn't as much reduction in the complexity as we would like to have seen. There was a lot of reduction when the House passed the bill initially By the time the Senate got their pause on it and it passed through there and literally you needed to get this vote and that vote, you know, a single senator that could hold things up and some of the complexity got back into the code. That being said, even though it's still for businesses, not a whole lot less complex than it was, they're paying a lot less. And as far as individuals go, most individuals, it will be less complex than it was before. For example, a lot more people are going to be able to take the standard deduction now, which is doubled, by the way, than had to itemize in the past. And unless you're in a high tax state where it's not the federal taxes that are higher, it's the state taxes are higher, the odds are you're going to be paying less taxes for a whole bunch of reasons. Now, for those folks who may live in traditional high tax states like New York and Illinois, And California, what I would encourage folks to do is don't complain about your federal taxes being too high. Complain about the state taxes, which are too high. That's what the real problem is. And those tend to be Democrat controlled states. So they need to argue with their Democrat state office holders to get their taxes down.
